question:
Each cell in the attached spreadsheet represents a plot of land. The color of the cell indicates who owns that plot. Green cells are plots owned by Earl Smith. Can Earl walk through every plot he owns (and no other plots) and return to his starting plot without backtracking? For this question, consider backtracking to be any instance where Earl would enter a plot of land he had already entered since leaving his starting plot.

Note: the task is to visit each owned plot exactly once and return to start without stepping onto non-owned plots.

Next: build an orthogonal adjacency graph and compute degree parity and connectivity. Code to run:

from collections import defaultdict, deque

green_cells = [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 2), (3, 5), (3, 6), (4, 2), (4, 6), (5, 2), (5, 6), (6, 2), (6, 6), (6, 7), (7, 2), (7, 6), (7, 7), (8, 2), (8, 3), (8, 6), (8, 7), (9, 3), (9, 6), (9, 7), (10, 3), (10, 6), (10, 7), (11, 3), (11, 5), (11, 6), (11, 7), (12, 3), (12, 5), (12, 6), (13, 2), (13, 3), (13, 5), (13, 6), (14, 2), (14, 5), (14, 6), (15, 2), (15, 5), (15, 6), (16, 2), (16, 3), (16, 4), (16, 5), (16, 6)]

cell_set = set(green_cells)

def build_graph(cells):
    g = defaultdict(list)
    for r,c in cells:
        for dr,dc in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]:
            nr,nc = r+dr, c+dc
            if (nr,nc) in cell_set:
                g[(r,c)].append((nr,nc))
    return g

graph = build_graph(green_cells)

# connectivity via BFS
start = green_cells[0]
visited = set([start])
q = deque([start])
while q:
    u = q.popleft()
    for v in graph[u]:
        if v not in visited:
            visited.add(v)
            q.append(v)

connected = (len(visited) == len(green_cells))

# degree parity
degrees = {node: len(neigh) for node,neigh in graph.items()}
odd_nodes = [node for node,deg in degrees.items() if deg % 2 == 1]
print("Connected:", connected)
print("Odd-degree count:", len(odd_nodes))
print("Sample degrees:", list(degrees.items())[:10])

Computer_terminal, please execute.
